test_cases.description: LoadSpec with a valid spec directory reads all required artifacts and returns a populated Spec struct with nil error.
preconditions: A valid spec directory exists at testdata/valid_spec/ containing prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, and tasks.json with well-formed content
test_cases.expected: Returns (*Spec, nil) where Spec has non-nil Requirements, TestSpec, Tasks, and PRD fields populated from the files
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, err = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); assert err == nil; assert spec != nil; assert spec.Requirements != nil; assert spec.TestSpec != nil; assert spec.Tasks != nil; assert spec.PRDBody != ""

test_cases.description: LoadSpec parses YAML frontmatter from prd.md using yaml.Unmarshal and populates all frontmatter fields on the returned Spec.
preconditions: A valid spec directory exists at testdata/valid_spec/ with a prd.md that has YAML frontmatter delimited by --- containing spec_id, spec_name, status, created_at, updated_at, owner, source, schema_version fields
test_cases.expected: Returns (*Spec, nil) with SpecID, SpecName, Status, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, Owner, Source, SchemaVersion fields populated from the YAML frontmatter; PRDBody contains only the Markdown body after the closing ---
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, err = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); assert err == nil; assert spec.SpecID == expectedSpecID; assert spec.SpecName == expectedSpecName; assert spec.Status == expectedStatus; assert spec.PRDBody does not contain "---"

test_cases.description: LoadSpec succeeds and leaves the architecture field empty when architecture.md is absent from the directory.
preconditions: A valid spec directory exists at testdata/no_arch_spec/ containing prd.md, requirements.json, test_spec.json, and tasks.json but NO architecture.md
test_cases.expected: Returns (*Spec, nil) with all required artifacts populated and Architecture field set to empty string
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, err = LoadSpec("testdata/no_arch_spec"); assert err == nil; assert spec != nil; assert spec.Architecture == ""

test_cases.description: Spec.Save writes all artifacts atomically via temp-then-rename and produces byte-for-byte identical output to the original fixture files.
preconditions: A valid spec loaded from testdata/valid_spec/ into a Spec struct
A writable temporary directory tmpDir exists
test_cases.input: spec.Save(tmpDir) where spec was loaded from testdata/valid_spec/
test_cases.expected: Returns nil; files in tmpDir are byte-for-byte identical to files in testdata/valid_spec/ for all artifacts; no temp files remain in tmpDir
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, _ = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); err = spec.Save(tmpDir); assert err == nil; for each artifact file: diff = cmp.Diff(readFile("testdata/valid_spec/"+name), readFile(tmpDir+"/"+name)); assert diff == ""

test_cases.description: Spec.Save on a sealed Spec returns a LifecycleError without writing any files.
preconditions: A Spec struct with Status set to 'sealed'
A writable temporary directory tmpDir exists
test_cases.expected: Returns a LifecycleError (non-nil); no files are created in tmpDir; errors.As(err, &LifecycleError{}) returns true; errors.As(err, &SpecError{}) returns true
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = createSealedSpec(); err = spec.Save(tmpDir); assert err != nil; assert errors.As(err, &LifecycleError{}); assert errors.As(err, &SpecError{}); assert len(listFiles(tmpDir)) == 0

test_cases.description: MarshalJSON serializes struct fields in declaration order and sorts all map[string]T keys alphabetically.
preconditions: A Requirements struct with a glossary map containing keys in non-alphabetical insertion order (e.g., 'zebra', 'apple', 'mango')
test_cases.input: MarshalJSON(requirementsStruct) where glossary map has keys inserted as ['zebra', 'apple', 'mango']
test_cases.expected: Returns ([]byte, nil); the JSON output has glossary keys in alphabetical order: 'apple', 'mango', 'zebra'; struct fields appear in declaration order matching JSON Schema property order
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: data, err = MarshalJSON(req); assert err == nil; parsed = jsonParse(data); keys = getKeys(parsed.glossary); assert keys == ["apple", "mango", "zebra"]; assert fieldOrderMatchesDeclaration(data)

test_cases.description: MarshalJSON produces byte-for-byte identical output to the Python library for every spec artifact type including nested structs and map fields.
preconditions: Golden fixture files in testdata/ produced by the Python afspec library for each artifact type (requirements.json, test_spec.json, tasks.json)
test_cases.input: MarshalJSON(artifact) for each artifact loaded from testdata/valid_spec/
test_cases.expected: The returned []byte is byte-for-byte identical to the corresponding golden fixture file content
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: for each fixture in testdata/valid_spec: artifact = loadArtifact(fixture); data, err = MarshalJSON(artifact); assert err == nil; diff = cmp.Diff(readFile(fixture), data); assert diff == ""

test_cases.description: Spec.Validate on a fully valid spec returns a ValidationResult with Valid true and empty Errors slice.
preconditions: A Spec loaded from testdata/valid_spec/ that passes all schema and cross-file checks
test_cases.input: spec.Validate() where spec is fully valid
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: true, Errors: []} (Errors slice is empty or nil); Warnings may be non-empty
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, _ = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); result = spec.Validate(); assert result.Valid == true; assert len(result.Errors) == 0

test_cases.description: Spec.Validate on a spec with errors returns a ValidationResult with Valid false and a non-empty Errors slice.
preconditions: A Spec struct with at least one schema violation (e.g., a requirement missing a required field)
test_cases.input: spec.Validate() where spec has a schema error
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [...]} where Errors has at least one entry
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildInvalidSpec(); result = spec.Validate(); assert result.Valid == false; assert len(result.Errors) > 0

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateSchema on a structurally valid spec compiles bundled schemas via SchemeURLLoader and returns ValidationResult with Valid true.
preconditions: A Spec loaded from testdata/valid_spec/ that conforms to all bundled JSON Schema files
Bundled schema files are embedded in the binary via //go:embed
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateSchema() where spec is structurally valid
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: true} with no errors
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, _ = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); result = spec.ValidateSchema(); assert result.Valid == true; assert len(result.Errors) == 0

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateSchema maps each *jsonschema.ValidationError to a ValidationResult error entry with InstanceLocation as path, KeywordLocation as keyword, and Message as description.
preconditions: A Spec with requirements.json that violates the JSON Schema (e.g., a requirement missing the required 'id' field)
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateSchema() where requirements artifact fails schema validation
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [{path: <InstanceLocation>, keyword: <KeywordLocation>, message: <human-readable>}]}
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildSchemaViolatingSpec(); result = spec.ValidateSchema(); assert result.Valid == false; assert len(result.Errors) > 0; err = result.Errors[0]; assert err.Path != ""; assert err.Message != ""

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateCrossFile on a spec with consistent cross-file references returns ValidationResult with Valid true.
preconditions: A Spec loaded from testdata/valid_spec/ where all test entries reference existing requirement IDs and all IDs follow the expected format
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateCrossFile() where all cross-file references are consistent
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: true} with no errors
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, _ = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); result = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); assert result.Valid == true; assert len(result.Errors) == 0

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateCrossFile records a dangling reference error when a test entry references a non-existent requirement ID.
preconditions: A Spec where test_spec.json contains a test case with requirement_id 'XX-REQ-999' that does not exist in requirements.json
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateCrossFile() where a test entry has a dangling requirement reference
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: false, Errors: [{category: 'integrity', check: 'dangling_reference', message: contains 'XX-REQ-999'}]}
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildSpecWithDanglingRef("XX-REQ-999"); result = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); assert result.Valid == false; err = findError(result.Errors, check="dangling_reference"); assert err != nil; assert err.Category == "integrity"; assert contains(err.Message, "XX-REQ-999")

test_cases.description: ValidateCrossSpec checks API symbol consistency, glossary conflicts, and contract mismatches across all provided specs using the dependency graph.
preconditions: Two Spec values with compatible glossaries and no conflicting API symbols
A DependencyGraph with an edge from spec A to spec B
test_cases.input: ValidateCrossSpec([specA, specB], graph) where specs are compatible
test_cases.expected: Returns ValidationResult{Valid: true} with no errors
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: result = ValidateCrossSpec([specA, specB], graph); assert result.Valid == true; assert len(result.Errors) == 0

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateStructured on a valid spec returns a map with 'valid' true, 'errors' as empty slice, and no 'warnings' key.
preconditions: A Spec loaded from testdata/valid_spec/ that passes all validation checks with no warnings
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateStructured() where spec is fully valid with no warnings
test_cases.expected: Returns map[string]any{"valid": true, "errors": []map[string]any{}}; the map does not contain a 'warnings' key
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec, _ = LoadSpec("testdata/valid_spec"); result = spec.ValidateStructured(); assert result["valid"] == true; assert len(result["errors"].([]map[string]any)) == 0; _, hasWarnings = result["warnings"]; assert hasWarnings == false

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with schema errors returns a map with 'valid' false and 'errors' entries containing 'category', 'message', and 'artifact' fields.
preconditions: A Spec with a schema violation in requirements.json (e.g., missing required field)
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateStructured() where spec has a schema error
test_cases.expected: Returns map with 'valid' false; 'errors' slice has at least one entry with 'category'=='schema', non-empty 'message', and non-empty 'artifact' string
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildSchemaViolatingSpec(); result = spec.ValidateStructured(); assert result["valid"] == false; errors = result["errors"].([]map[string]any); assert len(errors) > 0; e = errors[0]; assert e["category"] == "schema"; assert e["message"] != ""; assert e["artifact"] != ""

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with integrity errors returns a map with 'valid' false and 'errors' entries containing 'category'=='integrity', 'message', and 'check' fields.
preconditions: A Spec with a cross-file integrity violation (e.g., a dangling requirement reference in test_spec.json)
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateStructured() where spec has an integrity error
test_cases.expected: Returns map with 'valid' false; 'errors' slice has at least one entry with 'category'=='integrity', non-empty 'message', and non-empty 'check' string
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildSpecWithDanglingRef("XX-REQ-999"); result = spec.ValidateStructured(); assert result["valid"] == false; errors = result["errors"].([]map[string]any); e = findEntry(errors, "category", "integrity"); assert e != nil; assert e["check"] != ""; assert e["message"] != ""

test_cases.description: Spec.ValidateStructured on a spec with warnings includes a 'warnings' key with entries containing 'category'=='warning', 'message', and 'entity_id' fields.
preconditions: A Spec that passes validation but triggers at least one warning (e.g., a requirement with no test coverage)
test_cases.input: spec.ValidateStructured() where spec has warnings but no errors
test_cases.expected: Returns map with 'valid' true; 'warnings' key is present and contains at least one entry with 'category'=='warning', non-empty 'message', and non-empty 'entity_id'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = buildSpecWithWarnings(); result = spec.ValidateStructured(); assert result["valid"] == true; warnings = result["warnings"].([]map[string]any); assert len(warnings) > 0; w = warnings[0]; assert w["category"] == "warning"; assert w["message"] != ""; assert w["entity_id"] != ""

test_cases.description: Spec.Transition with a valid target state updates the spec status, persists to disk, and returns the updated Spec.
preconditions: A Spec with Status 'draft' saved to a writable temporary directory tmpDir
test_cases.expected: Returns (*Spec, nil) where returned spec.Status == "active"; the prd.md in tmpDir reflects the new status
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = createDraftSpec(); updated, err = spec.Transition("active", tmpDir); assert err == nil; assert updated != nil; assert updated.Status == "active"; savedSpec, _ = LoadSpec(tmpDir); assert savedSpec.Status == "active"

test_cases.description: ValidTransition returns true for allowed transitions and false for disallowed ones with no side effects.
test_cases.expected: ValidTransition("draft", "active") returns true; ValidTransition("draft", "sealed") returns false; ValidTransition("sealed", "draft") returns false; no files are written, no state is mutated
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: assert ValidTransition("draft", "active") == true; assert ValidTransition("active", "sealed") == true; assert ValidTransition("draft", "sealed") == false; assert ValidTransition("sealed", "draft") == false; assert ValidTransition("active", "superseded") == true; assert ValidTransition("sealed", "superseded") == true

test_cases.description: Spec.Supersede on a sealed spec transitions to superseded, prepends a deprecation banner to the PRD body, and persists to disk.
preconditions: A Spec with Status 'sealed' saved to a writable temporary directory tmpDir
test_cases.expected: Returns (*Spec, nil) where returned spec.Status == "superseded" and spec.PRDBody starts with a deprecation banner referencing spec ID '02'; the prd.md in tmpDir reflects these changes
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: spec = createSealedSpec(); updated, err = spec.Supersede("02", tmpDir); assert err == nil; assert updated.Status == "superseded"; assert startsWith(updated.PRDBody, deprecationBannerContaining("02")); savedSpec, _ = LoadSpec(tmpDir); assert savedSpec.Status == "superseded"

preconditions: A spec directory at tmpRoot/01_myspec/ containing valid spec artifacts

test_cases.description: DiscoverSpecs scans a root directory for NN_snake_case subdirectories and returns SpecMeta entries with all fields populated.
preconditions: A root directory containing subdirectories 01_first_spec/ and 02_second_spec/ each with valid prd.md files
test_cases.expected: Returns ([]SpecMeta, nil) with two entries; each entry has non-empty SpecID, SpecName, Status, and Dir fields matching the prd.md frontmatter
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: metas, err = DiscoverSpecs("testdata/workspace"); assert err == nil; assert len(metas) == 2; for each meta: assert meta.SpecID != ""; assert meta.SpecName != ""; assert meta.Status != ""; assert meta.Dir != ""

test_cases.description: BuildDependencyGraph reads tasks.json for each spec, extracts cross-spec dependencies, and returns a DependencyGraph with Edges, Dependencies, Dependents, and TopologicalSort methods.
preconditions: Two SpecMeta entries for specs '01' and '02' where tasks.json of spec '02' declares a dependency on spec '01'
test_cases.expected: Returns (*DependencyGraph, nil); graph.Edges() returns at least one DependencyEdge with FromSpec='02' and ToSpec='01'; graph.Dependencies('02') returns the edge; graph.Dependents('01') returns the edge
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: graph, err = BuildDependencyGraph([meta01, meta02], "testdata/workspace"); assert err == nil; assert graph != nil; edges = graph.Edges(); assert len(edges) >= 1; assert edges[0].FromSpec == "02"; assert edges[0].ToSpec == "01"

test_cases.description: DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort on an acyclic graph returns spec IDs in topological order where each spec appears before its dependents.
preconditions: A DependencyGraph with edges: 02->01 (02 depends on 01) and 03->02 (03 depends on 02)
test_cases.input: graph.TopologicalSort() on an acyclic graph with edges 02->01 and 03->02
test_cases.expected: Returns (["01", "02", "03"], nil); '01' appears before '02', '02' appears before '03'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: order, err = graph.TopologicalSort(); assert err == nil; assert indexOf(order, "01") < indexOf(order, "02"); assert indexOf(order, "02") < indexOf(order, "03")

test_cases.description: DependencyGraph.TopologicalSort on a graph with a cycle returns nil and an error identifying the cycle.
preconditions: A DependencyGraph with a cycle: spec '01' depends on '02', spec '02' depends on '01'
test_cases.expected: Returns (nil, error) where error message identifies the specs involved in the cycle (e.g., contains '01' and '02')
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: order, err = graph.TopologicalSort(); assert order == nil; assert err != nil; assert contains(err.Error(), "01") || contains(err.Error(), "02")

test_cases.description: LoadSpecLandscape with includeArchive true scans all spec directories including archive and excludes the currentSpecID entry.
